title: Tonix Pharmaceuticals Announces Publication in the Peer-Reviewed Journal of Virology Assessing Virulence of the 2022 Outbreak Strain of Mpox in New Animal Models

analysis.time: Publication date: July 15, 2026. Event date: The research was conducted at Tonix and the paper was published in the Journal of Virology on July 15, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: United States (research conducted at Tonix's Research and Development Center in Frederick, Maryland). Animal models: CAST/EiJ mice (7- to 8-week-old and 4- to 5-month-old) and three novel C57BL/6 mouse models deficient in interferon-α receptor, interferon-γ receptor, or both receptors. Human population: Mpox affects mostly men who have sex with men in the U.S., where it has become endemic.
analysis.event: Tonix Pharmaceuticals announced the publication of a peer-reviewed paper in the Journal of Virology titled 'Monkeypox virus clade IIb isolate exhibits reduced virulence relative to clade IIa isolates in multiple murine models.' The study assessed the virulence of the 2022 outbreak strain (clade IIb) compared to the historic 2003 clade IIa using new animal models.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study demonstrated that the emerging clade IIb isolate is up to 100,000-fold less virulent than clade IIa isolates. Case fatality rates differ among subclades: Ia (~11%), Ib and IIa (~4%), and IIb (~0.2%). The decreased virulence of clade IIb may have contributed to its ability to spread worldwide. Indolent subclinical infection is a risk factor for unintentional spread.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The research was conducted at Tonix's state-of-the-art research laboratory capabilities, including a Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) lab and an Animal Biosafety Level 3 (ABSL-3) facility. Tonix is advancing TNX-801, a live, attenuated, minimally replicative investigational vaccine candidate based on horsepox virus, to protect against mpox disease. The manuscript is accessible at https://doi.org/10.1128/jvi.00247-26. The study provides valuable new tools for rapidly investigating the pathogenesis of emerging MPXV subclades and evaluating medical countermeasures, including vaccines.

analysis.brief_en: On July 15, 2026, Tonix Pharmaceuticals announced the publication of a peer-reviewed study in the Journal of Virology comparing the virulence of the 2022 mpox outbreak strain (clade IIb) to the historic 2003 clade IIa. The research, conducted at Tonix's facilities in Frederick, Maryland, utilized new murine models, including CAST/EiJ and interferon-deficient C57BL/6 mice, to demonstrate that clade IIb is up to 100,000-fold less virulent than clade IIa. Case fatality rates vary significantly among subclades, with IIb at approximately 0.2%. The study highlights the risk of indolent subclinical infection for unintentional spread and provides new tools for investigating mpox pathogenesis and evaluating vaccines like Tonix's TNX-801.

title: 2024年布隆迪布琼布拉猴痘(mpox)的流行病学特征与传播动力学 - 生物通

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-21. Event date range: 2024-07-25 to 2024-10-26 (study period); epidemic progression observed from 2024-06-13 to 2024-10-26.
analysis.location_and_population: Population: 850 laboratory-confirmed mpox cases and 7,773 confirmed contacts. Demographics: Median age 20.3 years; 71.9% aged <5 years and 16–29 years; 38.8% pediatric (<16 years), 33.1% young adults (16–29 years). Occupations: Students (34.8%), merchants (14.0%), sex workers (4.7%), drivers (4.1%).
analysis.event: A research article published in the Journal of Infection and Public Health analyzing the epidemiological characteristics and transmission dynamics of mpox in Bujumbura, Burundi, during 2024. The study is a prospective cohort study conducted at three designated treatment centers.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 850 confirmed cases and 7,773 contacts (217 progressed to infection). Median hospitalization 10 days. Basic reproduction number (R0) estimated at 1.21 (95% CI: 1.11–1.31). Secondary attack rates: 14.0% among sexual contacts, 13.0% among household contacts. Transmission primarily via sexual contact (58.6%) and household exposure (38.6%). The outbreak peaked at 25 cases/day in August 2024. Risk: Sustained community transmission with moderate R0, affecting children and young adults; high HIV co-infection noted among sex workers (59.1%).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study is a retrospective analysis of existing data; no current active response status is described. Limitations include under-reporting, recall bias, incomplete genomic coverage, and potential selection bias due to mandatory hospitalization. The source is a full original report body.

analysis.brief_en: A prospective cohort study published in the Journal of Infection and Public Health analyzed mpox transmission in Bujumbura, Burundi, from July to October 2024. The research included 850 confirmed cases and 7,773 contacts, revealing a median age of 20.3 years with a high proportion of children and young adults. The study found sustained community transmission with a basic reproduction number (R0) of 1.21, driven primarily by sexual contact (58.6%) and household exposure (38.6%). Secondary attack rates were 14.0% among sexual contacts and 13.0% among household contacts. No deaths were reported, though 59.1% of sex workers were HIV-positive. The outbreak peaked in August 2024 and declined afterward. The authors recommend targeted interventions in sexual networks and households, alongside enhanced community monitoring and cross-border regional cooperation.

The research included 850 confirmed cases and 7,773 contacts, revealing a median age of 20.3 years with a high proportion of children and young adults. The study found sustained community transmission with a basic reproduction number (R0) of 1.21, driven primarily by sexual contact (58.6%) and household exposure (38.6%). Secondary attack rates were 14.0% among sexual contacts and 13.0% among household contacts. No deaths were reported, though 59.1% of sex workers were HIV-positive. The outbreak peaked in August 2024 and declined afterward. The authors recommend targeted interventions in sexual networks and households, alongside enhanced community monitoring and cross-border regional cooperation.

The virus spreads through close physical contact, including skin-to-skin, intimate, sexual contact, and contact with contaminated materials. Symptoms include fever, headache, muscle aches, swollen lymph nodes, tiredness, and a painful rash or skin lesions. The risk is elevated due to the increase in cases compared to the previous year.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WA health authorities have issued a fresh warning and are encouraging awareness, condom use, early testing, and vaccination.
